mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen monotonically for three consecutive weeks (-16.3, -16.0, -15.1, -11.6), a momentum that carries forward: the same reopening pull that lifted retail in the last three weeks continues into the next four, so the next 28-day mean exceeds the last.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose in each of the last three weekly means
failure_condition: The next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is at or below the last 28-day mean despite three prior consecutive week-on-week gains in RETAIL_REC.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has improved in each of the last three weeks (-51.3, -49.3, -45.7, -42.0) but remains deeply depressed; the gap between transit recovery and retail recovery means transit users are substituting local retail trips, and continued transit normalization will pull additional discretionary trips into RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean rises above -45.0 percent-change (i.e., improves past that level)
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 9.3 points over the four-week window
failure_condition: TRANSIT continues to improve past -45.0 while the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC falls below the last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility rebounded sharply from -28.9 to -17.4 and then -16.4, indicating a partial return to commuting; returning commuters generate lunch-hour and after-work retail spending that raises RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks in a two-step lag.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES weekly mean improves by more than 5 points within two weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES jumped 11.5 points from t-2w to t-1w
failure_condition: The next two weekly means of RETAIL_REC do not both exceed the last observed weekly mean of -11.6 after a WORKPLACES improvement of more than 5 points.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS swung from -21.0 to -7.1 within one week while RESIDENTIAL fell from 7.9 to 5.9, a pattern consistent with a seasonal weather break that shifts people out of parks and into indoor commercial venues, temporarily boosting RETAIL_REC over the next one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 10 points week-on-week while RESIDENTIAL falls at least 1 point over the same week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved +13.9 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: In weeks where PARKS rises more than 10 points and RESIDENTIAL declines, the following weekly RETAIL_REC mean is lower than the prior weekly mean.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent drawdown in RESIDENTIAL (9.6, 9.3, 7.9, 5.9) shows households progressively abandoning stay-at-home behavior; because residential entrenchment suppresses out-of-home consumption, its decline mechanically releases spending into RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined 3.7 points across the four-week window
regime_hint: any regime with declining residential mobility
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL declines again over the next four weeks yet the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is below the last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has stayed flat and modestly positive (3.3, 1.7, 3.4, 2.7) while RETAIL_REC rose, showing that essential-goods demand is saturated and non-essential capacity is the binding constraint; as restrictions ease further, that released capacity flows to RETAIL_REC, so the next four-week mean is higher.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains within +/-2 points of its four-week mean of +2.8
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM range over four weeks was only 1.7 points
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM stays within +/-2 points of +2.8 while the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is at or below the last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC's improvement is decelerating (+0.3, +0.9, +3.5 weekly increments) while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES gains are also flattening, indicating the reopening impulse is exhausting itself; the next four weeks therefore mean-revert lower relative to the last four.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT week-on-week improvement falls below 2.0 points
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT gained only 3.7 points from t-2w to t-0w versus 2.0 points from t-3w to t-2w
failure_condition: TRANSIT weekly improvement stays under 2.0 points yet the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC exceeds the last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime where WORKPLACES has recovered more than 10 points off its trough (-28.9 to -16.4), the marginal office return substitutes for leisure shopping trips, and the negative substitution dominates: RETAIL_REC falls over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES weekly mean sits above -18.0 while RESIDENTIAL falls below 6.5
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose 12.5 points from its four-week low while RESIDENTIAL fell to 5.9
failure_condition: Under WORKPLACES above -18.0 and RESIDENTIAL below 6.5, the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC exceeds the last 28-day mean.
